messages:
charlie_cust: Hey team — hitting a production blocker. We call Redwood API in JSON mode with a jsonschema validator on our side (pydantic) and about ~3% of responses fail with a 500 because the model returns invalid JSON. Example response breaks our parser.

jen_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the failing response + minimal repro? Also which Redwood endpoint (hosted/dedicated/private) and SDK/language?

charlie_cust: Hosted. Python requests -> pydantic model. Minimal request: POST /v1/generate with body: {"model":"x-large","mode":"json","schema":{...},"prompt":"generate user object"} Response we got (exact):
```
{
  name: 'Ava',
  email: "ava@example.com", // user email
  id: 12345,
}
```
This is invalid JSON (unquoted key, trailing comma, single quotes, inline comment). pydantic json loads throws ValueError -> we return 500 to our customers.

matt_eng: Thanks — that output definitely looks like the model didn't adhere to strict JSON. A couple quick thoughts: 1) Can you confirm you used temperature=0 and system prompt limiting verbosity? 2) Are you using the structured/json mode with schema enforcement turned on server-side, or only client-side validation?

charlie_cust: We set temperature=0 and included the JSON schema in the request body. We believed Redwood's JSON mode would enforce schema. Most responses are fine but we get intermittent drift.

sara_ml: Intermittent drift often comes from decoding issues or the model prefacing text. Two approaches: (A) upstream — force the model to only output JSON via additional system message + explicit "only reply with JSON matching schema" and function-calling if available; (B) downstream — tolerant parser fallback that tries to repair common issues (convert single->double quotes, remove trailing commas/comments, quote unquoted keys). We use a small tolerant sanitizer for customers.

matt_eng: For a short-term fix we can add a recommended sanitizer snippet in support docs. Example (Python):
```python
import re, json
from json import JSONDecodeError

def tidy(s):
    s = re.sub(r"//.*?$", "", s, flags=re.M)         # strip // comments
    s = re.sub(r"'(.*?)'", r'"\1"', s)            # single->double quotes (naive)
    s = re.sub(r",\s*\}(?=\s*$)|,\s*\]", lambda m: m.group(0).replace(',', ''), s)
    return s

try:
    data = json.loads(tidy(response_text))
except JSONDecodeError as e:
    raise RuntimeError(f"schema parse failed: {e}")
```
Note: this is heuristic and can silently change content; doc with caveats needed.

jen_support: Can you reproduce a minimal call we can run internally? If you can drop a cURL with API key redacted that would speed triage. Also we should capture the raw model text and the request payload for engineering.

charlie_cust: cURL (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-xlarge-1","mode":"json","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"},"name":{"type":"string"},"email":{"type":"string"}},"required":["id","name","email"]},"temperature":0}'
```
Raw response body attached above.

kevin_pm: From product — we should do two things: 1) add clearer docs / code snippets about downstream sanitizers and function-calling recommendation; 2) track a metric for "schema_parse_failures" exposed in the Console so teams can see noisy regressions. Also we should decide whether Redwood should attempt a server-side lenient parse fallback and return a structured error with both raw_text + parse_hint. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

matt_eng: Engineering notes: server-side lenient fallback is doable but has risk of silently mutating customer data (e.g., dates or numeric strings). Prefer we return a structured error object like:
```json
{
  "error":"schema_validation_error",
  "message":"failed to parse model JSON output",
  "raw": "<original text>",
  "suggestions": ["try temperature=0","use function-calling","see sample sanitizer"]
}
```
That gives customers context and we can add a Console link to auto-open a support ticket with the raw text attached.

sara_ml: Also worth noting model-switch: some model families adhere to stricter JSON output. We should add recommended model versions for structured output on the docs table (latency/strictness tradeoff). Add a note about prompt token windows causing truncation -> partial JSON + trailing commas.

jen_support: Action items: 1) @matt_eng please triage root cause (sampling/decoder/postprocessing) and confirm whether our JSON-mode enforces serialization or only prompts the model. 2) @matt_eng + @sara_ml propose error payload and Console telemetry (schema_parse_failures). 3) Support will share sanitizer snippet in docs and send customer a temporary workaround. 4) Product (@kevin_pm) to scope docs + telemetry.

matt_eng: Ack — I'll create an internal ticket with the thread and the raw response. Putting this on next sprint triage.

charlie_cust: Thanks, appreciate the quick help. We'll try the sanitizer for now and await your follow-up.

jen_support: Noted — I'll follow up once eng confirms ETA. :thumbsup:
